channels_note: mono, except arena-crowd-loop which is stereo
loop_crossfade: Leading silence below -50 dBFS is removed from every cue (5 ms detection window). Loop cues also have trailing silence below -50 dBFS removed, because a dead tail cannot meet the head. The last X seconds are then faded out on a quarter-sine curve and mixed at unity gain with the first X seconds faded in on the same curve. That mix becomes the head and the untouched middle (from X to duration minus X) is appended, so the file is X seconds shorter than the trimmed take. The last sample of the middle is the sample just before the old tail, and the first sample of the mix is that tail at full level, so the waveform continues across the loop point while the content eases from the end back to the start. X is 0.080 s (3840 samples) for the short loops and 0.250 s (12000 samples) for arena-crowd-loop.
